key_insight: MAGIC learns to build mixed-granularity multi-agent collaboration graphs by choosing, for each role, whether to use a single agent or a reusable group and how to connect it to the rest of the organization.
engineering_relevance: This lets practitioners tailor agent organizations to task complexity while improving reuse and inference efficiency in LLM-based multi-agent systems.
method: Sequentially constructs the graph one functional role at a time.
Selects each role as either a fine-grained agent or a coarse reusable group.
Uses dense-reward RL with potential-based shaping from probe-based utility and structural signals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art performance across eight benchmarks and a strong efficiency study.
watch_item: Training relies on reward shaping and sampled trajectories from a combinatorial search space, so probe design and reward balance may affect stability and transferability.
paper_title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
